label: UFactory 850
_comment_frames: THREE FRAMES ARE IN PLAY. Getting them confused is the single most
expensive mistake in this project, so every angle below states its own.
configurejoints : what the Configure Joints SOP and FBIK limits use
extracted       : what extract_angles() measures from the rest pose
robot           : what the controller and the CSV file speak
Every limit in this file is in the ROBOT frame, because that is the one
the published datasheet uses. Code converts to the other frames using
rig.sign and rig.offset_deg -- never hand-write a converted number.
Note that where sign is -1 the min and max SWAP under conversion.

rig._comment_axis: Measured, not assumed: dot(row, joint_5->joint_6 link) == 1.000 on the Y row.
rig._comment_sign: robot = extracted * sign. Only J3 is inverted on this rig.
rig._comment_offset: extracted = configurejoints + offset. Measured by pinning each joint to a narrow band and reading the extractor: J3 came back +90.5 against a +-0.5 probe band, so the true offset is 90.
rig._comment_fbik: FBIK enforces joint limits on J1/J2/J3/J5 but IGNORES them on J4 -- verified at +-5, +-30 and [60,70] with byte-identical output, and again here: pinning J4 to -20 and +20 both yielded -84.51, a slope of exactly 0. Rotation WEIGHTS do bind on J4 (1.0 -> 352 deg travel, 0.3 -> 101, 0.1 -> 26, 0.0 -> locked), so constrain J4 through weight, not range. Root cause unexplained.

output._comment_cap: Matches xarm-blender-animation core/csv_export.py, which sets max_speed_cap = 50.0 'for safety'. The Houdini asset shipped with 100, which only diverges once motion is fast enough for the cap to engage.

presets._comment: Robot frame. Converted to the configurejoints frame at apply time. J4 is absent because FBIK ignores its limits -- see rig.fbik_enforces_limits.
